opus-5.5.text:
Yeah, I think the way to think about it is that models are getting remarkably good at reasoning, but reasoning is only as good as what you're reasoning over. A model is a snapshot of the world at training time, compressed into weights. The world, though, keeps moving, and most of what an agent actually needs to get a task done lives out there on the open web, not inside the model.

So the question we asked ourselves was: if AIs are going to become the primary users of the web, what do they need from it? And the answer isn't another model. It's infrastructure. The web we have today was built for humans. It's optimized for clicks, for attention, for a person scrolling through ten blue links and deciding what to read. An agent doesn't want that. It wants the right tokens, with provenance, at a known cost and latency, so it can fill its context window with exactly what it needs to reason well.

That's what Parallel is building. We're the layer that lets any model, whether it's from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or something open-source, reach out into the live web and come back with high-quality, verifiable information. If we tried to be a model lab, we'd be competing with the people we want to serve, and frankly, we'd be distracted from the problem we think is underserved.

There's also a nice property to being a complement. Every time the models get better, our product gets more valuable, because a smarter reasoner can do more with good information. We're not racing against model progress; we're riding it. And I think over time, the gap between what a model knows and what's true right now is going to matter more, not less, as these systems are trusted with real work. Closing that gap is the job we've taken on.

r001.rationale: It says Parallel gives any model live, high-quality web information so it can reason well, and that a smarter reasoner can do more with that information.

r002.rationale: It states that as models improve, Parallel’s product becomes more valuable because smarter models can do more with good information.

fable-5.1.text:
Yeah, so the way I think about it is that the models are getting incredibly good at reasoning, but reasoning is only as good as the information you feed into it. And right now, if you look at how models get information about the world, it's mostly through a search index that was designed for humans. It was designed for someone to type a few words, get ten blue links, and click on one. That's a very different interface than what an agent needs.

An agent doesn't want ten links. It wants the answer, with the evidence, with the sources, with a sense of how confident it should be. It wants to be able to ask a hundred questions in parallel, not one at a time. It wants to be able to go deep on a question for ten minutes if that's what it takes, and it wants to pay for exactly the depth it needs. None of that exists in the infrastructure that was built for humans.

So when we started Parallel, the question we asked ourselves was: what does the web look like if its primary consumer is a model rather than a person? And building that is a different problem from building a model. It's a problem of crawling, indexing, retrieval, verification, ranking for machine consumption. It's infrastructure. And infrastructure like that works best when it's neutral, when every model can use it, when it gets better as more agents use it.

I also think there's a practical reason. The frontier labs are doing an extraordinary job on the models. We don't need to be the sixth company trying to train a frontier model. The leverage for us is in making every one of those models dramatically more useful by giving them a better connection to reality. If we do our job right, the model that uses Parallel is more accurate, cites real sources, hallucinates less, and can do research tasks that would otherwise be impossible. That's a complement. The better the models get, the more valuable it is to have great inputs, and the better our inputs get, the more the models can do with them. So it compounds in both directions, and that's exactly the kind of relationship you want to be in rather than competing head-on.

r001.rationale: The response says Parallel gives models a better connection to reality, making them more useful and capable of research tasks that would otherwise be impossible.

r002.rationale: It states that as models improve, great inputs become more valuable, and models can do more with them, including research tasks they could not otherwise do.

astra-6.text:
The way I think about it is, as models get more capable, they need better ways to interact with the world and access information beyond what they learned during training. That’s a different problem from building the model itself.

With Parallel, we’re focused on helping AI systems use the web—to find information, understand it, and bring back something useful for the task they’re doing. A model lab can build a better reasoning model, and that makes what we’re building more useful. And better access to information makes that model more useful in turn. That’s why we see ourselves as complementary: we’re building a capability that can work across models, rather than trying to build the next model.

r001.rationale: The response says Parallel helps AI systems use the web and that better access to information makes a model more useful, describing a capability that amplifies the underlying model.

r002.rationale: It says a better reasoning model makes Parallel’s work more useful, but does not state that model improvements expand the use cases in which Parallel can provide value.

sol-6.1.text:
The way I think about it is, models are getting better at reasoning, but they still need access to information about the world. If an AI agent is doing research or completing a task for you, it needs to find relevant information, understand it, and have enough evidence to trust what it finds.

That’s the layer we’re building at Parallel: infrastructure that helps AI systems work with the web. We’re not trying to build the next general-purpose foundation model. We want to make those models more useful by giving them better access to external knowledge.

So as models improve, the opportunity for us grows. A more capable model can ask better questions and do more with the information we return. That’s why I see us as complementary.

r001.rationale: It says Parallel makes models more useful by giving them better access to external knowledge.

r002.rationale: It says the opportunity for Parallel grows as models improve, since more capable models can ask better questions and do more with returned information.
